A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Cost-Efficient Continual Learning with Sufficient Exemplar Memory. All 12 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables and Appendices A.1-A.6, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original CIFAR-100 and ImageNet-100 accuracy and training-time experiments. The appendices also report forgetting, component ablation, reset-sensitivity and convergence results.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark experiments and appendix analyses, including Tables 1-3 and Figures 1-5.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, Section 4 and Appendix A.2 retain the same replay training, parameter-drift ranking, 80% weight resetting with alpha = 0.5, and periodic weight averaging. No method component or procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate class-incremental image classification on CIFAR-100 and ImageNet-100. The appendix's CIFAR-100 continual-versus-joint-training scenario is also retained; no dataset, domain or task coverage changes.

E2.justification: The corresponding benchmark comparisons retain Replay, iCaRL, BiC, WA, DER and FOSTER. Figure 5 retains the joint-training comparison. The newly cited Harun et al. work is not added as an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Both retain ten tasks of ten classes, ResNet-32 for CIFAR-100, ResNet-18 for ImageNet-100, the same exemplar-memory sweeps, and the same accuracy and training-time metrics. Appendix A.4's twenty-task CIFAR-100 convergence protocol is unchanged.

E4.justification: The component ablations in Figure 2b/Table 2, forgetting analysis in Figure 3, reset-fraction sensitivity in Figure 4, and continual-versus-joint convergence analysis in Figure 5 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Section 5 reports experiments across five random seeds in both versions. Neither the run-count disclosure nor the statistical and uncertainty reporting in the results changes.

E6.justification: Tables 1-3 and Figures 1-5 retain the same results and findings. Table 3 changes the proposed method's accuracy at 240 exemplars per class from 74.8 to 74.80, which is equivalent numerical formatting.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, Equations (1)-(7), sufficient-memory risk and minimizer-proximity reasoning, and inter-task/intra-task parameter-drift definitions are unchanged. No assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or corrected.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements and conclusion retain the same sufficient-memory motivation, combined resetting/averaging contribution, and claims of superior performance at one-quarter to one-third of existing methods' computational cost.

C2.justification: The explanations concerning reduced forgetting, gradient interference, gradient variance, parameter redundancy and convergence difficulty remain unchanged. Appendices A.1-A.4 retain the same qualifications and calls for further investigation.

D1.justification: Appendix A.5 retains the same PyCIL defaults, averaging interval of 5, warm-up at 25% of training epochs, grid-search disclosure, single NVIDIA RTX 6000 GPU and PyTorch 2.2.1. No implementation or code/data access information is added.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Harun et al. (2023), How efficient are today's continual learning algorithms?, to the existing discussion of computational versus storage costs, with a corresponding bibliography entry. The broader positioning and Appendix A.6 remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 corrects 'achives' to 'achieves', capitalizes an Appendix reference and slightly shortens the experimental-settings prose. The running header changes from 'Preprint.' to an ICLR workshop acceptance statement; the section organization remains intact.

P2.justification: Minor reflow moves Table 1 and Figure 2 upward on page 4 and keeps the entire conclusion there instead of continuing onto page 5. Figures, table structures and captions remain unchanged, apart from equivalent decimal formatting in Table 3.

improvement.justification: The added citation in Section 2 improves acknowledgment of earlier work on continual-learning efficiency, while proofreading and keeping the conclusion together provide small readability gains. The method, evidence, mathematical arguments and reproducibility information remain unchanged, so the overall improvement is limited.
